note: A1+ Unit 1 Lesson 1.10 built on 2026-11-18 under the A1+ lesson standards approved 2026-10-27 and the user's 2026-11-09 rule that every A1+ lesson follows up the A1 lesson with the same number. A1 1.10 Pets names four pets and says what each is doing (The dog is running.). The user chose its as A1+ 1.10's one grammar step on 2026-11-18 and asked for Unit 1 to be completed straight to Preview. Each of the four friends has a pet, and the pet has its own thing: Luis's dog Max plays with its ball in the park, Sofia's cat Luna is on its bed, Diego's bird Rio drinks its water in its cage, and Ana's rabbit Coco eats its food in her garden. What is its name? asks about the pet; his and her stay for people (His name is Luis. / Its name is Max.). English speakers often call their own pet he or she, so its is never set against his or her about the same pet: a wrong option names the person in the photo instead, and the Listen text cards are about what was heard. Four new Flash photos (b01-b04).

lesson.title: 1.10 What is its name?
lesson.unit_outcome: Describe people and family, say what people do every day and how often, and ask about other people’s habits.
lesson.goal: Ask and say a pet's name with its (What is its name? Its name is Max.) and say what a pet does with its things (The dog plays with its ball.), next to his and her for people.
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.10 Pets: A1 names four pets and says what each is doing (The dog is running.); A1+ 1.10 gives each pet a name and its own things. The one new grammar relationship is its, the possessive for an animal or a thing, next to A1's his and her for people: What is its name? Its name is Max. / His name is Luis. / The dog plays with its ball.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 1.10 dog, cat, bird, rabbit, pet; A1 3.1 What is your name? and name; A1 3.10 his and her; A1 3.12 have; A1 4.2 bed; A1 5.2-5.3 food and water; A1 7.13 ball; A1+ 1.2 drinks, eats; A1 4.8 play.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say its with a short i and a clear final ts (its name), different from his (with h and a z sound); ask What is its name? with falling intonation. Do not require native-like speed.
